newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries rally may hurt 3-year note auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries rally may hurt 3-year note auction.

text.p: Tuesday morning's big rally in the U.S. Treasury market puts the success of this afternoon's three-year note auction in jeapordy, market participants said.
The Treasury, at 0100 EST/0600 GMT, is slated to sell $18.5 billion in three-year notes.
But with the when-issued notes dropping to 5.87 percent, traders said it will be a miracle to find decent demand.
"To me, it doesn't pay to own three-year notes at these levels," said Jim Kenney, head trader at Prudential Securities Inc.
Traders said they expect the yield on the three-year note to come in at 5.88-5.89 percent -- still above where players had hoped.

"I never thought they'd be at this level," Kenney said, adding that on Monday, he figured they would be in the low 5.90-percent range. He said he would not invest in three-year notes that yield only 5.87 percent, "especially with 5-1/4 percent (Fed) funds and no change in Fed policy."
As such, traders anticipate a small backup ahead of the note sale, but not enough to find buyers.
"There was no interest yesterday when they were at 5.92 percent, and there's certainly no interest down a nickel at 5.87 percent," said Mike McClure, head trader at Zions First National Bank.

He noted that most of the buying in Treasuries Tuesday has been in the longer end, with hedge funds buying bonds. "There's been some outright buying," McClure said, "but it's mostly selling Canada and buying U.S., and selling Europe and buying U.S....Three years have been dragged along."
Still, traders don't expect a disastrous auction. "It won't go horribly," a trader said, "but retail will back away because of too high levels." That ensures a dealer-driven auction, she added.
"It'll be a mixed-bag because Election Day will add to the tentativeness," she said.

Non-competitive bids are seen around $800 million, although some see it around $650-700 million. And the bid to cover ratio is seen less than the 2.5 average the past 24 three-year note auctions, at 2.3.
